items.t: Silver Valley is a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood governed by its own area plan inside the Official Community Plan (OCP).
The City publishes no street-level boundary for the board sub-area, so no exact boundary line is stated here.
Kanaka Creek runs along the area's south and east side, with Kanaka Creek Regional Park following the creek corridor.
The plan organises growth as hamlets rather than one continuous subdivision, which is why street patterns break at creek and forest edges.

blocks.text: Silver Valley: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Silver Valley Area Plan was modernised by an amending bylaw adopted November 25, 2025, replacing the 2002 plan structure with simplified designations and a zoning matrix.
Properties in the wildfire interface need a Wildfire Development Permit, or a restrictive covenant with wildfire construction requirements where an exemption applies.
Wildfire rules require a minimum 10-metre setback from the top of ridgelines, cliffs or ravines unless a hazard assessment justifies a change.
Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 states RS-1 subdivision minimums of 668.0 m² lot area, 18.0 m width and 27.0 m depth, maximum lot coverage 40%.

blocks.text: Silver Valley: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The district bus change is the detail most families miss: Silver Valley/Rockridge Garibaldi students are expressly excluded from regular SD42 transportation.
Kanaka Creek Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park, not a City park, so its rules and hours come from Metro Vancouver.
The 2025 plan update was part of a citywide package aligning the OCP and the Town Centre, Hammond and Silver Valley area plans with provincial housing legislation.
A full OCP review is planned by 2030 using 2026 Census data, so current designations are not the final word for undeveloped parcels.

blocks.text: Silver Valley: development and new projects

items.t: The City is developing a new one-acre neighbourhood park in Silver Valley at 232A Street and Blaney Road.
The 2026–2030 Capital Plan funds safety improvements at Dewdney Trunk Road and 256 Street, including road widening, on the area's east-side route.

Area-specific cost here is servicing type, not a different tax rate: metered customers moved to seasonal water rates on January 1, 2026, with lower rates outside May to September and a lower fixed base rate.
Most Maple Ridge utility charges are billed on the annual property tax notice, while metered water and sewer customers receive a quarterly metered utility bill.
There is no rail station in Silver Valley; the city's West Coast Express stations are Maple Meadows and Port Haney, reached by road or bus.
TransLink's Langley–Haney Place bus rapid transit project is in detailed planning at 22 kilometres between Willowbrook and Haney Place, with designs, costs and timelines not yet determined.

blocks.text: Silver Valley: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the wildfire map first: the City's Wildfire Development Permit Area map decides whether a permit or covenant applies to the lot.
Check creek setbacks second: the City's floodplain bylaw designates land near watercourses as floodplain and sets floodplain setbacks, with the greatest applicable setback governing.
The floodplain open-house material names steep creeks such as Kanaka Creek as a fast-water and sediment hazard during heavy rain — relevant to ravine lots here.

faq.q: Is Silver Valley on a current area plan or an old one?
faq.a: A current one governs it. Council adopted the updated Silver Valley Area Plan on November 25, 2025; the City says the update modernises the 2002 plan, consolidates land-use designations, adds a zoning matrix and adds density required by provincial legislation, so buyers should read the 2025 plan text, not summaries of the old plan.

faq.q: Does the wildfire permit area change how a house must be built?
faq.a: Yes, it can change materials and landscaping. The City requires a development permit for development in mapped wildfire risk areas, and its construction sheet requires ember protection on vents and ignition-resistant treatment for decks, balconies and overhangs; some small projects proceed only with a covenant recording those requirements instead.

faq.q: Is there a school bus for Silver Valley secondary students?
faq.a: No regular district bus serves that trip now. SD42 lists regular transportation only for named catchments including Whonnock Elementary and Garibaldi Secondary excluding students residing in the Silver Valley/Rockridge area, and the district states those Silver Valley routes were discontinued in the 2025/26 budget for low ridership and available public transit alternatives.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Silver Valley?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 46 houses listed with 5 sold in the month and 13 condos and townhomes listed with 2 sold in the month in Silver Valley. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Silver Valley a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 11%, a buyers’ market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 15%, a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
